title: Illuminating the dark kinome utilizing multiplex peptide activity arrays to functionally annotate understudied kinases

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states that schizophrenia samples were from "schizophrenia (16, M:8 and F:9) subjects." The stated sex counts sum to 17, not 16. This makes the reported cohort size internally inconsistent and must be corrected.

The protocol says homogenates were "spun down at 13×G for 15 min at 4°C" before separating supernatant from pellet. Centrifugation at 13 times gravity is not a plausible clarification spin for pelleting tissue debris in this workflow; 13,000×g is likely intended. As written, this is a materially erroneous and nonreproducible protocol.

The INSRR construct is reported as residues L24-A747. Human INSRR is a type-I receptor tyrosine kinase whose cytoplasmic catalytic kinase domain lies C-terminal to the transmembrane region, well beyond residue 747. This reported construct is extracellular-domain material and lacks the catalytic kinase domain, so it cannot intrinsically phosphorylate PamChip peptides as an INSRR kinase. Any observed signal cannot be interpreted as INSRR kinase activity without correcting the construct identity/range or demonstrating a different active construct.

The reported LTK protein spans residues S20-P424. Full-length human LTK is a receptor tyrosine kinase with its catalytic cytoplasmic kinase domain C-terminal to this range (approximately beginning after the transmembrane region, around residue 470 or later). The stated protein is therefore an extracellular-domain fragment lacking the kinase domain, yet it is treated throughout as an active recombinant tyrosine kinase. This invalidates the claimed LTK peptide-phosphorylation profile unless the material/range is corrected.

predicted_errors.error_location: Human schizophrenia PamChip comparison and downstream enrichment analysis
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Individual human lysates were pooled "by sex and diagnosis," producing only four pooled samples, and each pool was run in technical triplicate. Technical replicates of one pooled lysate are not biological replicates and cannot support inference about control-versus-schizophrenia differences or sex-specific LFCs. Nevertheless, the manuscript calculates comparative LFCs, selects differential peptides, and calls enrichment results significant. Pooling also prevents estimation of between-subject variability and makes the stated subject-level case/control comparison non-identifiable.

The abstract claims "195 novel kinase-substrate interactions," but the described evidence is phosphorylation of short immobilized reporter peptides on a PamChip. Peptide phosphorylation, especially in a purified-enzyme array, does not establish that the cognate full-length cellular protein is a direct physiological substrate or that a kinase-substrate interaction exists in cells. Only EPHA6/GAB1 is described as receiving follow-up validation, so the broad substrate-interaction claim substantially overstates the assay evidence.

predicted_errors.error_location: Recombinant-screening clustering and Abstract references to "affinity"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The manuscript labels peptides as "high," "medium," and "low affinity" solely according to the lowest tested recombinant-protein concentration at which phosphorylation is detected. No kinetic binding or catalytic parameters (for example, Km, Kd, kcat, or initial-rate fits) are measured. Detection threshold in a concentration-response array is not affinity, so all affinity terminology and conclusions about variable degrees of affinity are unsupported and misleading.

The abstract reports 195 novel kinase-substrate interactions. The Results report 53 peptide hits for EPHA6 (18 high + 31 medium + 4 low), 65 for AATK (9 + 46 + 10), 15 for INSRR (3 + 4 + 8), 5 for LTK (3 + 1 + 1), and 63 for TNK1 (26 + 31 + 6), totaling 201 kinase-peptide hits. The paper provides no explanation for why the headline count is 195 rather than 201 or what exclusions were applied.

Figure 3 identifies the screened kinase as "EPHA8" and lists "EPHA8_Medium Affinity," whereas the text, abstract, materials, and Results consistently identify EPHA6 as the screened Eph receptor. EPHA8 was not included among the five stated kinases. This is a target-identification error in a central selectivity/overlap figure, not merely cosmetic nomenclature.
